comments.text: Note different verb form used before まい.
comments.html: Note different verb form used before まい.

comments.text: Hmm, not completely sure of the translation on this one ...
comments.html: Hmm, not completely sure of the translation on this one ...

comments.text:
そうです。日本語があまい！How about this?

君から、もし構わなければ、この話を先生に相談してくれまいか？
comments.html:
そうです。日本語があまい！How about this?
君から、もし構わなければ、この話を先生に相談してくれまいか？

comments.text:
Did you pick up the translation from Google? Searched by よろしく相談。The sentence is from a letter written in 1916. The Japanese is old.

…、この話を先生に相談していただけませんか？or 相談していただけないものか？ would be modern expression.
comments.html:
Did you pick up the translation from Google? Searched by よろしく相談。The sentence is from a letter written in 1916. The Japanese is old.
…、この話を先生に相談していただけませんか？or 相談していただけないものか？ would be modern expression.

comments.text: まいか or ないか is normally used by a senior person to address his junior. It is not a honorrific.頂けませんか would be the polite form.頂けないものか would be the mordern version of まいか.
comments.html: まいか or ないか is normally used by a senior person to address his junior. It is not a honorrific.頂けませんか would be the polite form.頂けないものか would be the mordern version of まいか.

comments.text:
I was taught that this まいか form is also used to express some confusion : whether...or not -- don't know yet. 

...行こうか行くまいか考えている。

..still considering whether going or not.
